title: Introduce epoched KV snapshots and soft-backpressure for batcher handoffs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: long-tail latency spikes and periodic stalls in the continuous batching path are correlated with synchronous KV index compaction and cross-shard handoffs. The current eviction/compaction approach creates stop-the-world phases for hot shards and forces the batcher to block while leases are reconciled. This ticket implements an epoched snapshot approach for the KV cache plus a soft-backpressure layer on the batcher handoff path to smooth contention. Goals: reduce 95/99p latency spikes, eliminate 1-3s stall events during compaction, and enable safer dependency upgrades (RocksDB/LMDB) without prolonged GC pauses.

Proposed solution:
- Introduce lightweight epoched snapshots for KV shards: writers advance epoch numbers and snapshot compaction works on an immutable epoch snapshot to avoid blocking reads.
- Background compaction worker that operates on old epochs and writes compacted segments, with an atomic swap into the shard index.
- Soft-backpressure mechanism in the batcher: admit requests into a fast-path token window and route overflow to a scored wait-queue prioritized by latency SLO and token age. This replaces the current hard-blocking lease wait in many code paths.
- Lock-free read path for common-case KV reads: use epoch validation and compare-and-swap to avoid global shard locks.
- Add migration shim to keep old eviction/compaction behavior available behind a feature flag for gradual rollout.
- Upgrade embedded storage library from rocksdb-6.x -> rocksdb-8.2 to take advantage of low-latency compaction knobs. Add compatibility layer to avoid index layout regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- 99th percentile tail latency for standard generation workload reduced by at least 30% in the canary region.
- No increase in error rate or token drop.
- Successful canary rollout in dedicated staging for 72h with full traffic replay.
- Automated migration tool that can rebuild compacted segment for a shard with <10s per shard median time.

Why this is different from prior work: many previous tickets focused on rebalancing, eviction tuning, or decoupling interfaces. This work changes the compaction semantic to 'epoch snapshots + atomic swap' and introduces a prioritized soft-backpressure admission that aims to reduce latency variance without sacrificing throughput. It also bundles the storage upgrade and provides a migration path to avoid mass rebuilds at deploy time.
comments: 2025-11-04 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage. Observed correlation in prod logs between 'compaction-start' events and batcher stalls. Collected sample traces and flamegraphs. See Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/KV+Epoch+Snapshots+Proposal

2025-11-12 - Miguel Ortega: Design review notes — prefer epoch validation over RCU for now to keep complexity bounded. Raised concern about compatibility when upgrading RocksDB; request for a compatibility test harness.

2025-12-02 - Eng Arch (Lena Brooks): Approved overall approach; suggested we add a 'safety margin' in backpressure thresholds to account for cold caches. Assigned follow-up: define metrics and SLO gating for canary (ENG-314159-META).

2026-01-20 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented prototype of epoched snapshot and background compactor. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1789. Prototype shows <5% throughput impact and 40% fewer stalls in synthetic slot contention test.

2026-02-05 - QA (Tom Winters): Integration tests added. Found a race in shard swap during leader failover — added a fencing token to the atomic swap. Test case linked: https://internal-ci.redwood.ai/job/kv-epoch-swap/

2026-02-18 - Perf (Rina Gupta): Bench results on staging cluster (n3-large-gpu): baseline 99p=420ms, after prototype 99p=260ms with no throughput loss for standard text-gen workload. Attached dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-epoch/epoch-snapshots-bench
2026-03-01 - Security (Elaine Park): Reviewed storage upgrade plan. No PII migration implications; ensure KMS key rotation happens before compaction of encrypted segments. Added checklist item.

2026-03-07 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented soft-backpressure queue and integrated admission scoring. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1964. Observed small increase in average latency (+4ms) but 20% fewer 1-2s stall incidents in long-run test.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Ortega: Running canary in eu-west-1 on runtime-1.31-bitbucket with feature-flag 'kv_epoch_snapshots' enabled for 5% of traffic. No errors after 48h; monitoring shows expected tail improvements. Next: enlarge to 25% and run 72h stability window.
